questions.question: In KL‑regularized control, what is the primary interpretation of the objective E[r(y)] − β KL(π||π_ref)?
questions.choice_A: A trade‑off between maximizing reward and staying close to a reference policy interpreted as a Bayesian posterior update
questions.choice_B: A purely entropy‑maximizing objective unrelated to probabilistic inference
questions.choice_C: A constraint that forces the policy to match the reference policy exactly
questions.choice_D: A Lagrangian relaxation that eliminates the need for any reward signal

questions.question: Under the soft‑optimality derivation, what role does the temperature parameter β play?
questions.choice_A: It scales the reference policy probabilities directly but not the reward
questions.choice_B: It controls the sharpness of the policy distribution by trading off exploitation of reward against adherence to π_ref
questions.choice_C: It enforces that the partition function equals one
questions.choice_D: It ensures the KL divergence is always zero

questions.question: Which expression correctly captures the soft/Gibbs form of the optimal policy in a single‑step setting?
questions.choice_A: π(y) ∝ exp(β r(y))
questions.choice_B: π(y) ∝ π_ref(y) r(y)
questions.choice_C: π(y) ∝ π_ref(y) \, \exp(r(y)/β)
questions.choice_D: π(y) ∝ \exp(r(y)) / π_ref(y)

questions.question: What is the partition function Z in the soft policy π(y) ∝ π_ref(y) exp(r(y)/β)?
questions.choice_A: The KL divergence between π and π_ref
questions.choice_B: The entropy of the reference policy
questions.choice_C: The expected reward under the reference policy
questions.choice_D: The normalizer Z = \sum_y π_ref(y) \exp(r(y)/β) that ensures π is a probability distribution

questions.question: How does the KL‑regularized objective connect to a constrained optimization viewpoint?
questions.choice_A: By viewing β as the Lagrange multiplier of a constraint KL(π||π_ref) ≤ \epsilon
questions.choice_B: By forcing π to be uniform over actions
questions.choice_C: By requiring the partition function to be bounded by \epsilon
questions.choice_D: By ignoring the reward and constraining only the KL

questions.question: When π_ref is uniform over actions, the KL‑regularized objective reduces to which familiar form?
questions.choice_A: Pure risk minimization without regularization
questions.choice_B: Maximum entropy reinforcement learning with entropy bonus β H(π)
questions.choice_C: Pure imitation learning of π_ref
questions.choice_D: A policy gradient objective without a baseline

questions.question: What is the soft value function V_soft(s) in terms of a soft Q function and π_ref?
questions.choice_A: V_soft(s) = \max_a Q(s,a)
questions.choice_B: V_soft(s) = \sum_a π_ref(a|s) Q(s,a)
questions.choice_C: V_soft(s) = β \log \sum_a π_ref(a|s) \exp(Q(s,a)/β)
questions.choice_D: V_soft(s) = Q(s,a^*) for a^* sampled from π_ref

questions.question: Which property of the log‑partition function A(r) = β \log \sum_y π_ref(y) \exp(r(y)/β) is most relevant for policy improvement?
questions.choice_A: It is linear in r
questions.choice_B: It is concave in r
questions.choice_C: Its gradient is zero at the optimum
questions.choice_D: Its gradient yields the soft‑optimal policy distribution over y

questions.question: What is a computational challenge of evaluating the partition function in large discrete action spaces?
questions.choice_A: It requires summing over all actions, which may be intractable without approximation
questions.choice_B: It cannot be estimated with any sampling method
questions.choice_C: It always diverges for bounded rewards
questions.choice_D: It depends only on state transitions, not on actions

questions.question: How does KL‑regularized control connect to probabilistic inference in trajectory space?
questions.choice_A: By equating rewards with negative log transition probabilities
questions.choice_B: By interpreting the optimal policy as the posterior over trajectories under an exponential‑tilted prior induced by π_ref
questions.choice_C: By treating the reference policy as a likelihood function
questions.choice_D: By removing the need for dynamics modeling

questions.question: In actor‑critic algorithms with soft value functions, what does the critic typically estimate?
questions.choice_A: The hard max value V(s) = \max_a Q(s,a)
questions.choice_B: The KL divergence between π and π_ref
questions.choice_C: A soft Q or soft V that uses log‑sum‑exp rather than hard max for bootstrapping
questions.choice_D: The gradient of the partition function with respect to β only

questions.question: Which identity expresses the change‑of‑variables between rewards and policies under the soft optimality condition?
questions.choice_A: r(y) = β \log π_ref(y) − β \log Z
questions.choice_B: π(y) = \exp(r(y))
questions.choice_C: r(y) = β \log \frac{π(y)}{π_ref(y)} + c, for some constant c that does not depend on y
questions.choice_D: π_ref(y) = β \log \frac{π(y)}{Z}

questions.question: What is the principal effect of decreasing β in the Gibbs policy π(y) ∝ π_ref(y) \exp(r(y)/β)?
questions.choice_A: The policy becomes more peaked around higher‑reward actions, approaching argmax behavior
questions.choice_B: The policy becomes more uniform
questions.choice_C: The policy ignores the reward and matches π_ref exactly
questions.choice_D: The partition function becomes independent of r(y)

questions.question: Which of the following is a practical implication of the soft control‑as‑inference perspective for reward shaping?
questions.choice_A: Reward shaping is impossible under KL regularization
questions.choice_B: Adding a potential‑based shaping term corresponds to a reparameterization that can be absorbed into π_ref or the baseline without changing optimal behavior
questions.choice_C: Reward shaping must always change the optimal policy
questions.choice_D: Reward shaping invalidates the partition function

questions.question: Why is the log‑sum‑exp operator central to soft value iteration?
questions.choice_A: It exactly computes the minimum over actions
questions.choice_B: It linearizes the Bellman operator
questions.choice_C: It provides a smooth, convex approximation to the max that arises from marginalizing an exponential family distribution
questions.choice_D: It removes dependence on the reference policy

questions.question: In continuous action spaces, which approach is commonly used to handle the partition function?
questions.choice_A: Direct enumeration of actions
questions.choice_B: Ignoring normalization completely
questions.choice_C: Using importance sampling, variational approximations, or reparameterized policies that make Z tractable or unnecessary to evaluate explicitly
questions.choice_D: Setting β to zero

questions.question: What does minimizing KL(π||π_ref^*) with π_ref^*(y) ∝ π_ref(y) \exp(r(y)/β) correspond to in policy improvement?
questions.choice_A: Projecting the current policy onto the soft‑optimal target distribution
questions.choice_B: Forcing the critic to be unbiased
questions.choice_C: Matching moments of the reward distribution only
questions.choice_D: Eliminating the entropy bonus from learning

questions.question: What is a key benefit of using soft value functions in actor‑critic learning?
questions.choice_A: They guarantee exact optimality in finite time
questions.choice_B: They reduce variance and provide smoother gradients by avoiding hard max operations
questions.choice_C: They remove the need for exploration entirely
questions.choice_D: They allow learning without any reward signal

questions.question: How can changes to the reference policy π_ref be interpreted in the control‑as‑inference framework?
questions.choice_A: As modifying the dynamics model
questions.choice_B: As changing the prior over actions, which shifts the soft‑optimal policy without altering the fundamental inference structure
questions.choice_C: As adding observation noise to rewards
questions.choice_D: As replacing the partition function with a constant

questions.question: Which statement best describes the duality between reward maximization and KL constraint in KL‑regularized RL?
questions.choice_A: Maximizing reward subject to a KL constraint is dual to minimizing KL subject to achieving a target soft value
questions.choice_B: Maximizing entropy is dual to maximizing reward without constraints
questions.choice_C: Minimizing KL is equivalent to setting β → ∞
questions.choice_D: There is no duality; the two views are unrelated

questions.question: Which gradient identity is most useful for deriving policy updates under the soft optimality model?
questions.choice_A: ∇_r β \log \sum_y π_ref(y) \exp(r(y)/β) = softmax_{π_ref}(r/β), the soft‑optimal policy over y
questions.choice_B: ∇_β r(y) = π(y)
questions.choice_C: ∇_r KL(π||π_ref) = 0 at all r
questions.choice_D: ∇_β KL(π||π_ref) = r(y)
